peer_results.rationale: While AMD is planning an acquisition with regulatory approval conditions, its 2024 disclosure focuses on the agreement to acquire ZT Systems and does not disclose any historical 2023 acquisition termination fees or specific 2023 litigation benefits/fines comparable to Intel's reported $1.2B benefit and $754M in charges.

comparisons.peer_summary: Restructuring and other charges recognized in operating expenses were $1,533 million in fiscal year 2024 and $244 million in fiscal year 2023. The 2024 charges primarily consisted of employee termination costs related to cost reduction activities associated with the VMware Merger, while the 2023 charges were primarily non-recurring charges related to IP litigation.
comparisons.comparison: Both Intel and Broadcom report specific non-recurring charges in their fiscal year 2023 results that impacted their operating expenses, though the nature of the charges differed. Intel recorded a $401 million EC-imposed fine and a $353 million termination fee in 2023, alongside a $1.2 billion litigation benefit. Broadcom similarly reported that its 2023 restructuring and other charges of $244 million were 'primarily included non-recurring charges related to IP litigation,' demonstrating a shared industry context of significant legal/regulatory and restructuring costs impacting reported results in the comparable prior year period.

sentences.text: In 2023, a $1.2 billion benefit was recorded due to the reduction in the previously accrued charge as a result of developments in the VLSI litigation.

2023 charges also included a $401 million charge for an EC-imposed fine and a $353 million termination fee in connection with our inability to timely obtain required regulatory approvals needed to acquire Tower Semiconductor Ltd. Refer to "Note 19: Commitments and Contingencies" within Notes to Consolidated Financial Statements for information about litigation related items.
Restructuring and other charges recognized in operating expenses were $1,533 million and $244 million in fiscal years 2024 and 2023, respectively.
The fiscal year 2023 charges primarily included non-recurring charges related to IP litigation.

peer_results.rationale: Micron's 2024 disclosures only reference general note locations for restructuring and contingencies; they do not provide specific 2023 monetary figures for litigation benefits or acquisition termination fees comparable to Intel's detailed accounting of the VLSI benefit and Tower/EC charges.

comparisons.peer_summary: Operating expenses increased in fiscal year 2024 due to employee growth and compensation increases; fiscal year 2023 included a $1.4 billion acquisition termination charge related to the proposed Arm transaction.
comparisons.comparison: Both Intel and NVIDIA disclose significant acquisition termination charges in their prior year (2023) results. Intel incurred a $353 million termination fee due to the failure to obtain regulatory approvals for its Tower Semiconductor acquisition in 2023. Similarly, NVIDIA's fiscal year 2023 results included a $1.4 billion acquisition termination charge related to the proposed Arm transaction. This highlights a common theme of M&A integration risks and associated non-cash charges impacting recent financial history for both companies.
